primary_decision_axis.label: which of the seven guests to accuse of the murder
primary_decision_axis.description: Having gathered what the clues and the guests' lies support, name one of the seven as the killer — with the Kernel insisting the wrong person must be a live, pickable option, not just the right one.

decision_mechanism.note: The Kernel names the accusation but not how often it occurs; the country-house whodunit conventionally resolves it at one culminating denouement, with everything before it as build-up — a fair-play solution also implies a single moment where the answer is committed to.

secondary_decision_axes.label: which guest's lie to press or which clue to follow next
secondary_decision_axes.description: At each investigative beat before the accusation, pick which of the seven lying guests to confront about their account, or which physical clue or red herring to run down, with the snowbound house limiting how much can be checked.
secondary_decision_axes.note: Not stated as a choice, but forced by seven guests each lying about something plus a stated mix of real clues and red herrings — the player must select where to spend attention; it is a distinct choice-shape (whom to question / what to pursue) rather than a refinement of the accusation, though it feeds into it.

decision_landscape.note: No direct relational statement, but "a fair solution" and "accuse the wrong person" together frame the investigation as the means by which the accusation is informed — the interrogation/clue choices elaborate toward the single stated accusation rather than standing as a co-equal pillar.
